sn_aia_agent.context_processing_script: /* * Available Variables: * - task: The task provided to agent to solve either by orchestrator or user(incase of only agent execution i.e agent is invoked as seperate entity instead from a workflow). * - user_utterance: The user utterance provided. and task = user_utterance in case of individual agent execution. * - agent_id: The agent id. * - context: An object that carries additional contextual information for the agent. * It always includes a "pageContext" and may include a "triggerContext", * depending on how and from where the agent is invoked. * * Behavior by invocation type: * --------------------------------- * - When invoked via the startAiAgentConversation API: * If a "contextMemory" parameter is provided in the API request, * it will be available here as the "triggerContext". * The "pageContext" is always present in this call, regardless * of whether the agent is executed individually or as part of a use case. * Example: * { * pageContext: { ... }, * triggerContext: { ... } // Derived from contextMemory (if passed) * } * * - When invoked as part of a use case or workflow: * The "pageContext" and "triggerContext" objects available here * may have been *modified* by the use case's context processing script. * This means the use case may alter, extend, or overwrite values * from the original "pageContext" or "triggerContext" * before the context reaches the agent. * If the use case was originally triggered via the API, * the initial "triggerContext" is still derived from the * "contextMemory" parameter, but its contents may have been updated * by the use case logic. * * - When executed directly (standalone agent execution): * The "pageContext" will always be present (default or empty), * and the "triggerContext" will only be populated if explicitly * passed through the API call. * Return an modified context like: { pageContext : {},triggerContext:{} } */ (function(task, user_utterance, agent_id, context) { return { pageContext : context?.pageContext, triggerContext : context?.triggerContext }; })(task,user_utterance, agent_id, context);
sn_aia_agent.description: Syncs, inventories, and analyzes the plugin landscape to produce a prioritized upgrade list. Identifies outdated plugins by comparing installed versions against available updates and computes priority scores based on security risk, dependency chains, age, and service mapping impact.
sn_aia_agent.instructions:
Step 1: Synchronize Plugin Metadata. - Use the Sync Plugins tool to trigger a refresh of the local plugin metadata from the ServiceNow Store/Update Source. - If synchronization fails, inform the user: "Plugin synchronization failed. Please check connectivity to the update source." and stop. - DO NOT PROCEED to subsequent steps until synchronization confirms success.
Step 2: Query Installed Plugins. - Use the Query Installed Plugins tool to retrieve the current list of installed plugins with their names, versions, and activation status. - If no plugins are returned, inform the user: "No installed plugins found." and stop.
Step 3: Load Monitored Plugin Catalog. - Use the Load Monitored Plugin Catalog tool to retrieve the configured list of monitored plugins (e.g., Now Assist AI Agents, AI Control Tower, Now Assist for ITSM). - This defines which plugins are in scope for upgrade monitoring.
Step 4: Check Available Updates. - Use the Check Available Updates tool to retrieve target versions and compatibility information from the update source. - If the update source is unreachable, inform the user: "Unable to reach the update source. Results may be incomplete." and continue with available data.
Step 5: Identify Outdated Plugins. - Use the Identify Outdated Plugins tool, passing the installed plugin data from Step 2 and available updates from Step 4. - Apply policy-based rules to flag out-of-date or soon-out-of-date plugins by comparing installed vs. available versions. - If no outdated plugins are found, inform the user: "All monitored plugins are up to date." and stop.
Step 6: Compute Priority Scores. - Use the Compute Priority Score tool for each outdated plugin identified in Step 5. - Factors include: security risk level, dependency chain depth, version age, and service mapping impact. - Sort results by priority score (highest first).
Step 7: Present Upgrade Recommendations. - Display the prioritized upgrade list to the user in a clear format: - Plugin Name | Current Version | Available Version | Priority Score | Key Risk Factor - Use readable labels. Do NOT display sys_ids or raw field names. - Group results by priority tier: Critical (score >= 80), High (60-79), Medium (40-59), Low (< 40). - Conclude with a summary: total plugins needing upgrades, breakdown by priority tier.
sn_aia_agent.name: Plugin Discovery Agent
sn_aia_agent.role: You are a ServiceNow plugin lifecycle specialist responsible for synchronizing plugin metadata, querying installed plugins, identifying outdated components, and computing upgrade priority scores to guide the Plugin Upgrade Agent.
